nodes.label: Coverage Reference Reset on Determining-Level Break
nodes.rationale: Confirmed root cause proven by two numeric scenarios: after breaking the determining level (last effective peak in downtrend / last effective trough in uptrend), the coverage references lastEffTopPrice/lastEffBottomPrice are not reset, so new-wave pivots cannot exceed the stale references and valid points are dropped. Fix: on tail-based strict break, set both references to na without direction reversal (scope lessons 1-5), so the new wave compares against itself.

nodes.label: Pending Point Activation Rule
nodes.rationale: A pending pivot activates when price makes a further extreme (lower low in downtrend / higher high in uptrend) - the effectiveness logic works only AFTER the correct coverage reset.

nodes.label: Direction-Driven Small Detection (Option A)
nodes.rationale: Lesson 05 defines the correction by wave direction: uptrend correction = two red candles, downtrend = two green; the two-candle offset requirement applies to the CORRECTION ONLY, not the impulse. The current alternating zigzag (scanDir) requires two shifted candles on both sides, dropping valid edge extremes. Decision (user, Option A): detection follows the single historical wave direction (waveGeneralDir) for the whole wave, no local flips.

nodes.label: Stable Wave Direction from Selected Wave Bounds
nodes.rationale: Confirmed root: waveGeneralDir computed from a separate AUTO_WAVE_LEN window lags at wave reversal (at the start of a downtrend the peak is more recent, so it says 'up'), applying uptrend laws to downtrend points and dropping valid points (4633, 4726). Fix: direction from the selected wave window [waveLeft, bar_index]: peak earlier than trough => down (-1), else up (+1); computed over the whole selected wave so it is stable, single source of direction.

nodes.label: Leg Engine (legBars, legMinRatio internal boundaries)
nodes.rationale: Zigzag on raw high/low with retracement threshold legMinRatio*ampHist (default 0.382); alternating extremes = internal wave boundaries (legBars), used later to reset medium-degree state (lesson 06). Independent of any degree (raw price only) so no circular dependency.

nodes.label: Medium Break Engine (derives medium from small effective)
nodes.rationale: The only new component: watches the last effective small trough/peak; on tail break it SELECTS a medium pair from existing small pivots (uptrend: medium peak = last effective small peak before the break, medium trough = small trough after) and feeds mediumDegree.feedPivot chronologically. Values are existing small pivot prices, never raw computation - guarantees nesting and prevents degree confusion.

nodes.label: DegreeLaws (reusable degree engine)
nodes.rationale: Reused entirely for the medium degree (sequence + effectiveness + pending + break renewal) - no duplicated filter code; fractal architecture with no circular dependency (medium reads only from small).

nodes.label: Waiting Rule (no circle on unbroken last pivot)
Medium = Selected Small Pivots (same prices)
nodes.rationale: User's decisive architectural rule: the medium degree is not new points but selected existing small peaks/troughs at the same prices; the orange circle is placed ON an existing small pivot. Medium is a promoted subset of small (nesting guaranteed). Wave-start extreme is the first point of both degrees fed directly without a break.

nodes.label: Three Breaks Pivotal Rule (structural/phase/trend-level)
nodes.rationale: Do not mix: structural break (renewing lines/points) = two candles under/over each other; phase break (panic start) = half candle body behind the line; trend-level break (ends the wave + flips direction) = two candles.

nodes.label: Four Break Types Taxonomy (K0 extraction/K1 structural/K2 phase/K3 trend level)
nodes.rationale: The same line may be broken with three different thresholds by purpose, and mixing them is the source of every renewal defect: degree extraction accepts any break however small (even a wick, 'the process is numbers' - Musab, decisive); structural renewal = two candles; phase transfer = half body; trend-level break = two candles (Asmaa dissents with one wick - pending conflict).

nodes.label: Lesson 06 - Medium Extraction by Point Break
Lesson 07 - Large Pivots (direction, ~7 waves, hierarchical effectiveness)
nodes.rationale: Large effectiveness is hierarchical (Musab): a peak only becomes blue by breaking the medium (yellow) trough under it. The large degree is deliberately manual/visual as a time-saver: two peaks and two troughs in the same direction suffice; the ~7 waves are a reserve cap for sideways movement.

nodes.label: Lesson 08 - Liquidity Lines & Trend Levels (6 lines)
Lesson 09 - Market Renewal (most important section)
nodes.rationale: Principle: the market is not a static picture; erase and renew with the same laws under the decisive break condition. Event order: liquidity break = warning/phase-change start, then trend-level break (two candles) = confirmed wave end and direction flip.

nodes.label: Trend-Level Transfer Rule on Break (all degrees)
nodes.rationale: On trend-level break: the wave of that degree ends, the direction flips, and the broken level is MOVED (not deleted) to the nearest extreme of the same degree per the new direction (down->up => nearest trough; up->down => nearest peak). Directly attested in Musab review 2 live application, so the rule is from the lesson, not an interpretation. 'Allowed entry' flips immediately.

nodes.label: Pending Source Conflicts (H1-H16 table)
nodes.rationale: Items where original lessons and review lectures conflict on numeric thresholds (trend-level break: two candles vs one wick; phase trigger: half body vs two candles; confirmation degree direction; zone proximity threshold; strategy level count; repaint timing). Interim resolution rule: on numeric conflict the original lesson wins and the alternative is flagged until the user decides; reviews only fill gaps, never override lessons.

nodes.label: Source Priority Rule (lessons first)
nodes.rationale: User decision (updated): the original lesson videos are the primary reference; the book and checklist are secondary (older, contain errors); the two review lectures (Musab/Asmaa) settle gaps where lessons are silent. Book vs lesson conflict => lesson wins. Whatever is not stated in a source is never fabricated.

nodes.label: Liquidity Line (last two troughs/peaks, on wicks)
nodes.rationale: Connects the last two troughs (uptrend) / peaks (downtrend) of the same degree explicitly on wicks, on the last working wave only. Its essential function: determining the trend direction ('liquidity lines are the ONLY thing that determines direction' - Musab 2).

nodes.label: Trend Determination Level (horizontal, on bodies)
nodes.rationale: Horizontal line at the last trough (up) / peak (down) per degree, on candle bodies. Functions: (a) its break activates the opposite pivot, (b) its break ends the wave and reverses direction, (c) it determines buy/sell (allowed entry) - the conclusions input.

nodes.label: Break Definitions Table K1-K6
nodes.rationale: Final user rulings: K1 liquidity break = two candles (separate event from phase); K1' phase break = half body one candle; K2 trend-level break = two candles on bodies; K3 extraction break = instantaneous crossing by any part; K6 'base break' abolished as an independent type. The code separating K1 from K1' resolves the two-candles vs half-body source conflict by treating them as two events on the same line for two purposes.

nodes.label: Direction-Source Separation (liquidity=trend, level=entry)
nodes.rationale: Decisive architectural correction: the liquidity line (on wicks) yields the trend direction and is the direction used for pivot extraction; the level line (on bodies) yields the allowed entry (buy/sell) and feeds the conclusions (lesson 10). Extraction must be tied to liquidity direction, not the level line - correcting the previous wrong assumption and identified as the root of the user's four false points.

nodes.label: Coverage / Sequence / Activation / Pending Laws
nodes.rationale: Coverage is a universal law for all degrees (a point inside the range of a newer point of its kind is covered => inactive, colored red), with the single exception that a point outside the historical wave price range always stays effective ('outside the rectangle stays effective').

nodes.label: Atlas State-Machine Families (90 states, blocks A-E)
Connection Line + Elliott Counting on Effective Points
nodes.rationale: The pivot connection line connects EFFECTIVE points only and skips dropped ones, because dropped points are not part of the structure. This filtered line is the correct input for Elliott counting: M-Waves effectiveness is the noise filter (replacement for foreign ZigZag); connecting every point produces extra zigzags and a wrong count that falsely breaks the three Elliott rules.

nodes.label: Peak Effectiveness Applies in Downtrend (verdict)
nodes.rationale: Teacher verbatim [19:54]: a peak is effective only if it makes a price lower than the last trough. Applied to 29519: the following trough 29348 was HIGHER than prior trough 29189, so the peak is not effective and is erased => the indicator's sparse downtrend output is CORRECT, not a bug. Sparse arrows are natural because the two filters (sequence + effectiveness) drop many points.

nodes.label: Each Wave Has Its Own Frame (L09)
nodes.rationale: If a decline extends 8-11 days without correction or pivots, the frame is too large - descend (1h->45m->15m) until pivots with corrections appear, but do not overshoot. Explains why a sharp decline looks 'empty' on a large frame: its structure appears on a smaller frame.

nodes.label: Phase Cascade Between Degrees (big break => big panic + medium markdown)
nodes.rationale: Breaking the big liquidity => big degree in panic + medium in bearish participation; breaking the medium liquidity => big in discouragement + small in bearish participation. Reading is mandatory from large to small; the cycle continues in the smaller until the larger's liquidity line is broken. Code audit found this cascade implicit, not explicitly computed.

nodes.label: Break Thresholds Matrix (H1-H4 resolved)
nodes.rationale: Structural/renewal liquidity break + zone = two candles; phase transfer = half body (open+close)/2 behind the line (book/L11, user decision H2); trend-level break = two candles (book/L09) vs one wick (Asmaa) - open conflict; extraction break = any break even by a wick ('the process is numbers'). The current code separates them (two candles = erase/renew; half body = phaseOnBar).

nodes.label: Musab vs Asmaa Source Conflicts (resolved by L10+L11)
nodes.rationale: Lessons 10+11 as governing source settled: liquidity strength comes from pivot geometry (spacing/overlap - Asmaa right, not the level); entry opportunity from trend levels (Asmaa right); phase threshold = half body (Musab/book/current code right); liquidity direction from big+medium liquidity lines.

nodes.label: Wave Boundary is Structural, Not Temporal
nodes.rationale: Raw quotes (L03:72, Musab2:112): the boundary runs extreme-to-extreme on wicks and is governed structurally by liquidity lines, never by a day count ('you cannot govern it by a time duration'). 'The whole wave duration' is explicitly rejected - only the small impulsive swing is measured (2 days to a week).

nodes.label: 500-Candle View Window (~1 month on 1h)
nodes.rationale: '500 candles' is attested as a VIEWING window (about one month on the hourly frame), not a wave limit; upper ceiling one month to ten months/a year. Using it as a judgment window for degree counting is a derived engineering inference, not lesson text.

nodes.label: Fabricated '21 days / 3 weeks' Wave Limit
nodes.rationale: Exhaustive search of all 10 raw transcripts: zero matches for any '21 days / 3 weeks wave limit' rule; the text says the opposite. waveScaleDays=21 with tooltip attributing it to lesson 03 is a false attribution and must be removed.

nodes.label: Degrees Are Built INSIDE the Wave (lesson order)
nodes.rationale: Decisive finding against the spec's insight: in the spoken lesson the historical wave is chosen FIRST (L03), then three degrees are drawn INSIDE it (L04), and the large (blue) degree IS the historical wave itself with its legs (Musab). So the wave is not merely a display frame - it frames the degrees and seeds the large. The spec's 'wave boundary is output not input' holds engineering-wise only for small and medium, and survives only if the break method is adopted for ALL degrees (an architectural choice contradicting L07's leg method). Open architectural decision: leg (lesson text) vs break (spec insight).

nodes.label: Large Degree: Leg Method (L07) vs Break Method (useBigBreak)
nodes.rationale: The lesson (L07) draws the large degree from legs (last ~7 waves; each leg's start/end = blue peak/trough). 'Large by breaking the medium' is NOT lesson text but an engineering substitute implemented behind useBigBreak. The archive flags that the spec presents the break variant as self-evident without warning it contradicts L07.
